newsitem.title: USA: Trans-World to invest $500 mln in Russian smelters.
newsitem.headline: Trans-World to invest $500 mln in Russian smelters.

text.p: Trans-World Group said it will invest $500 million to upgrade and expand output at two Russian aluminium smelters, Bratsk and Sayansk, in which the company has minority stakes.
David Reuben, Trans-World's executive chairman, told reporters that Bratsk would be expanded in two stages.
In the first stage, output would be raised from current production of 780,000 tonnes of aluminium metal a year to 810,000 tonnes.
After the second stage is completed within about two years, output will rise to 840,000 to 850,000 tonnes, Reuben said.
The money will be raised from banks by offsetting the additional metal produced, Reuben said.
At Sayansk production can be raised from current output of 350,000 tonnes a year to 420,000 to 430,000 tonnes a year without new infrastructure investment, Reuben added.

Trans-World will sell 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes of aluminum produced in Russia this year, Reuben said. "We will produce and purchase on a world wide basis some 1.5 million tonnes of aluminum," he added.
The company has previously said it would also expand alumina output.
Trans-World has a controlling stake in Kazakhstan's Pavlodar alumina refinery which is producing 1.1 million tonnes a year of alumina.
"What we want to do is to bring Pavlodar to 1.3 million tonnes a year," said James Viciana, senior vice president of Kazchrome International, a Trans-World majority-owned company.
Trans-World also has two bauxite mines near the Pavlodar refinery, and intends to build a new, one-million-tonne per year refinery at the same location.
Engineering studies have begun in a project that will take two to three years to complete. Some capital has been raised already, Viciana said.
Trans-World handles some 2.5 to three million tonnes of alumina a year, of which 1.1 million is produced at Pavlodar.
The company provides alumina for tolling into metal at Bratsk and Sayansk. Two tonnes of alumina are needed to produce one tonne of aluminium.
Reuben said Trans-World also has minority stakes in the Novokuznetsk smelter and Achinsk alumina refinery in Russia.

Reuben, along with other senior company officials and lawyers, briefed reporters Wednesday evening about their campaign to clear Trans-World's name of a series of allegations, some of which were repeated by Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov in a February 21 speed to the Duma (parliament).

Kulikov also suggested the Russian aluminium industry needed protecting from Western aluminium tolling companies by tighter federal controls, and also suggested duties should be slapped on raw materials imported to make aluminum.
Bratsk made an accumulated profit of about $300 million in 1995 and 1996, while Sayansk earned $8 to $12 million in the past year, Reuben said.
